judged_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a truthy string comparison, not a boolean flag, so '0', 'false', or 'no' all enable credential sharing. Operators following the .env.example pattern of empty-string/false-style toggles who set CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET="false" (or any non-empty sentinel) silently turn on credential sharing and the remote sync endpoint path, redirecting every OAuth token refresh across google-calendar, o365, zoom, webex, lark, hubspot, and zoho to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT; every other flag in constants.ts (e.g. IS_MAILHOG_ENABLED) uses === "1", so the next change to this file will likely copy the correct pattern and the behavioral cliff remains hidden until a self-hoster debugging refresh failures finds it.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/lib/constants.ts, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which yields a truthy string (or undefined), not a boolean check like `=== "1"`. As a result, setting either env var to any non-empty sentinel (e.g., "0"/"false") will still enable the feature. This flag is then used to gate the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) and the token refresh redirection logic (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), so the finding’s core claim about accidental enablement is directly supported by the diff.
